LESSON: PHONOLOGICAL AWARENESS

Grade: Grade 5
Subject: MANDARIN
Strand: Listening and Speaking
Topic 1.2: Phonological Awareness
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 3

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Phonological Awareness, part of Listening and Speaking in Grade 5 MANDARIN.

Key inquiry question: What strategies can you use to apply new words effectively?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. listen to a group of words and indicate rhyming and non-rhyming words cooperatively,

2. repeat saying the group of words that rhyme aloud,

3. create new words and phrases from the initials, finals and tones given,

4. repeat the vocabulrary related to nuclear family members from a recording,

5. use vocabulary acquired to introduce different family members using simple sentences (e.g. 我爸爸叫......; 我爷爷叫 ......),

6. ask and respond to questions on the titles and names of their nuclear family members in turns (e.g. 你姐姐叫什么名字 ? 我姐姐叫......),

7. research the similarities and differences in the family units in Kenya and China and share their findings with peers.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. listen to a group of words and indicate rhyming and non-rhyming words cooperatively,
2. repeat saying the group of words that rhyme aloud,
3. create new words and phrases from the initials, finals and tones given,
4. repeat the vocabulrary related to nuclear family members from a recording,
5. use vocabulary acquired to introduce different family members using simple sentences (e.g. 我爸爸叫......; 我爷爷叫 ......),
6. ask and respond to questions on the titles and names of their nuclear family members in turns (e.g. 你姐姐叫什么名字 ? 我姐姐叫......),
7. research the similarities and differences in the family units in Kenya and China and share their findings with peers.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Phonological Awareness together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Critical thinking and Problem solving: The learner develops researching skills as they compare and contrast family units in

Kenya and China.

● Learning to learn: The learner develops healthy relationships when they work collaboratively with their peers to categorise

rhyming and non-rhyming words.

Values:
Respect is enhanced as the learner understands and appreciates the diverse perspectives on the family unit in Kenya and China.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

Family dynamics: The learner becomes aware of the varied family structures in their own and other communities, providing

them with rich cultural insights.

Link to other learning areas:

• The learner links their learning to Kiswahili and English on the skill of manipulation of sounds to create new words or

variations.

• The learner can relate their learning to Religious Education on the concept of family units and their role in the community.
